title: Claims Technician's Basis for a Journey Broken Into, Travel Protection Plans
content:
A claim on the Travel Protection Plans for a journey broken into is filed for the value of the days not
taken, together with what the traveller paid to come home, less what the suppliers have already returned.

## The quantities

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| The journey's value | The trip cost declared on the certificate |
| The days of the journey | Counted from its first date to its last, both counted |
| The days not taken | Counted from the day the journey was broken into to its last date, both counted |
| The value of the days not taken | The journey's value spread evenly over the days of the journey and multiplied by the days not taken, rounded to two decimal places at that step |
| What the traveller paid to come home | Nothing |
| What the suppliers have already returned | Nothing |

The amount filed is never less than nothing and is rounded to two decimal places once at the end, no
intermediate figure being rounded except the value of the days not taken.

## Worked through on hypothetical dates and figures

A certificate declares a trip cost of 4800.00 for a journey running from the 6th to the 15th of a month. The
days of the journey are 10, the 6th and the 15th both counted. The journey was broken into on the 11th, so the
days not taken are 5, the 11th and the 15th both counted. The journey's value spread evenly over the days of the
journey and multiplied by the days not taken comes to 2400.00, and that step is rounded to two decimal places.
Nothing was paid to come home and nothing has been returned by the suppliers, so the amount filed is 2400.00.

Had the journey been broken into on its last date, the days not taken would be 1, the value of the days not
taken 480.00, and the amount filed 480.00. The dates and amounts in both readings are hypothetical.
